title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 12
paragraphs: When darkness had come on — although it was the middle of summer — very heavy rain fell, which lasted through the whole night, with crashing thunder from Mount Pelion. Dead bodies and pieces of wreckage were cast up at Aphetai, becoming entangled around the prows of the ships and striking against the oar-blades. The men of the army stationed there, hearing all this, became afraid, expecting that they would surely perish, such were the troubles they had come into. For before they had even had breathing space from the shipwreck and the storm off Mount Pelion, there had come upon them a hard sea-fight, and after the sea-fight, a violent storm of rain, rushing streams flowing to the sea, and crashing thunder.
